newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina to seek new accord with IMF in April.
newsitem.headline: Argentina to seek new accord with IMF in April.

text.p: The Argentine government will negotiate in April a three-year Extended Fund Facility with the International Monetary Fund (IMF), Finance Secretary Pablo Guidotti said Thursday.
Guidotti said an IMF mission was currently in Buenos Aires inspecting Argentine government accounts and announced the IMF would disburse $150 million dollars this month.
"The meeting we had was to verify the September goals, which have been met, and the December goals, which we will not have any problems complying with," Guidotti told reporters.
Guidotti said in the future he would seek Congress to endorse the government's agreements with the IMF.
"It would be good that Congress backs the agreements that will then guide government policy," he said.

Guidotti said that the Senate will pass the 1997 budget as was approved in the lower house of Congress. That is, with a $3.2 billion deficit for the year, some $200 million more than what the government had expected earlier in the year.
He added that the government's five percent growth prospects for 1996 could be surpassed.
